correctness.rationale: All distinct nonempty palindromic subsequences partition by numbers of ones k=0,1,2,3; the respective gap counts are z, T+1, a three-rectangle union of cardinality (r+1)(b+c+1)+E, and (r+1)(s+1). The case split a<=d vs a>d is exhaustive including equality. Uniform ordered gap compositions converge to the Dirichlet simplex; the homogeneous n² term is Phi. Exponential minimum independence and exact mixed integrals give E(Phi)=7/80 and Var(Phi)=2299/1209600, strictly positive. Separate direct subsequence-set verification passed all 3,876 three-one words through length 18; exact rational checks reproduce the moments. No finite computation is used as an all-length proof.

evidence: Mahalingam–Pandoh establish a Fibonacci-type unrestricted upper bound on distinct scattered palindromes and an alphabet-dependent extremum when q >= n/2; fixed binary alphabet q=2 for arbitrary n does not satisfy the latter condition.

Rubinchik–Shur Theorem 1.1 concerns distinct contiguous palindromic factors for iid random words and average order sqrt(n), whereas scattered subsequences here scale quadratically under uniform fixed-three-one sampling.

originality.rationale: Closest primary full texts and plausible broader bounds were compared at statement/implication level: scattered-subword reconstruction by set equality, unrestricted scattered-palindrome bounds and their three-marker inequalities, and iid contiguous-palindrome factor expectations do not imply this exact fixed-three-one count and conditional limit law. Published results and available prior claims were searched for aliases and equivalent parameters; no covering claim was identified, with residual risk of unindexed equivalent work.
residual_risks: An equivalent fixed-weight-three result might exist in unindexed literature, obscure sequence databases, or an appendix not revealed by available indexes.
The 2021 three-occurrence insertion bounds are related but not sharp equalities; a clever additional derivation from other published lemmas is not ruled out categorically.

value.rationale: The exact cardinality of distinct scattered palindromic subsequences is an established string-complexity invariant, and conditioning on a fixed number of markers is natural for sparse binary strings. The theorem determines it for every word in a full infinite family by a transparent collision-free structural partition, then determines its order-n² limit random variable with exact positive variance. This goes beyond a small table, trivial parameter substitution, or a routine upper bound; the nonconcentration result characterizes fluctuations not captured by an extremal statement.
